adapterMatrix.note: Adapter compatibility cells. Cells are generated from this section plus `probes`, `reactEpochs` and `pixiEpochs`; nothing lists a cell by hand. A cell names its adapters as data (artifact, entry, class), so a package-layout change edits rows here only. Exact React and Pixi versions come from the audited `probes` tuples.
adapterMatrix.rendererNote: Render backends a cell conformance run can use. Each backend is checked separately (never inferred from the other): the conformance suite runs once per backend the tier and the Pixi adapter both list, and test/renderer.ts fails any Pixi application that does not get the requested renderer. The Chromium flags that provide each backend come from the GPU profile of the run (`gpuProfiles`).

software.description: Software rendering, no GPU: WebGL is ANGLE on SwiftShader, WebGPU is Dawn on SwiftShader's Vulkan device, which Chromium exposes only as a fallback adapter (isFallbackAdapter true), as in the examples WebGPU smoke test. What CI runs, and what the 2026-10-10 record ran on.

hardware.description: A real GPU through the platform's default path (Metal on macOS, Direct3D on Windows): no SwiftShader or fallback flags, in a headed browser. The render check fails when a run lands on a software renderer or a fallback adapter. For contributors' machines; CI has no GPU.

pixi8.sameClassNote: Each entry binds the pixi.js module its own loader resolves, so ESM and CJS legitimately differ in Node (pixi-8 README, D6).

pixi7.rendererNote: Pixi 7 has no WebGPU renderer: its cells run on WebGL only, and WebGPU is not applicable to them.
pixi7.conformanceNote: Pixi 7 lacks the Pixi 8 scene capabilities pixi.graphics-context (no GraphicsContext) and pixi.renderer-destroy-options (Application.destroy takes removeView, a boolean): the runner skips those two scenarios and names the capability.
pixi7.sameClassNote: Each entry binds the pixi.js module its own loader resolves, so ESM and CJS legitimately differ in Node (pixi-7 README, D6).
pixi7.excludedNote: 7.4.0: the adapter's entry fails to import in Node ('Worker is not defined', a module-scope browser global in pixi.js 7.4.0; data-only probe). 7.4.1 was never published to npm (absent from the registry's versions and time map).

pixi8-names-rejected.reason: pixi.js 7.2's declarations import `colord/types`, which does not resolve (TS2307 in @pixi/color/lib/Color.d.ts, hidden by skipLibCheck), so `ColorSource`, and with it the `tint` of every display object, is `any`; an `any` instance member turns the adapter's mapped element props into an open record, so `label` (Sprite) and `context` (Graphics) are accepted. pixi.js 7.3.0 fixed the import, and these two @ts-expect-error assertions hold from 7.3.0 on; a 7.2 cell compiles the consumer without them and records that it did (cell.json typeAssertions). Runtime behaviour is unaffected.

expectedBlankRender.reason: An upstream pixi.js bug before 8.10 (pixijs/pixijs#11389, fixed by #11417, first released in 8.10.0): the WebGPU texture batch is sized from WebGL's MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS (32 on ANGLE/SwiftShader) while the WebGPU device keeps the default maxSampledTexturesPerShaderStage of 16, so the bind group layout and the batch pipeline are invalid and the canvas stays blank (reads [0,0,0,0]) although Pixi creates a WebGPU renderer and every conformance scenario passes. It is not specific to software rendering: any device whose WebGL texture-unit count exceeds its WebGPU per-stage limit is affected (upstream reports a Pixel 9 and Chrome on Ubuntu). Not in the adapters.

evidence.observed: Every React adapter and patch on each listed version (8 cells per version in the first 2026-10-10 record, 11 in 2026-10-10.2): Pixi created a WebGPU renderer and every conformance scenario passed, but the render check failed: the canvas copy and Pixi's extract read [0,0,0,0] and the screenshot shows the page instead of the red rectangle. The same cells pass on WebGL. Under a WebGPU validation error scope the device reports 'The number of sampled textures (32) in the Fragment stage exceeds the maximum per-stage limit (16). While calling [Device].CreateBindGroupLayout', then 'Invalid RenderPipeline "PIXI Pipeline"' and an invalid command buffer on every frame; Chrome logs these as console warnings and Pixi does not surface them.
evidence.adapter: Dawn on SwiftShader's Vulkan device: vendor google, architecture swiftshader, isFallbackAdapter true. No GPU in the machine.
evidence.cause: Before 8.10, Pixi sizes the batch (Batcher.defaultOptions.maxTextures, GpuGraphicsAdaptor, SdfShader) with getMaxTexturesPerBatch(), which reads WebGL's MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS (32 here), and requests the WebGPU device without requiredLimits, so maxSampledTexturesPerShaderStage stays 16. pixijs/pixijs#11417 (merge 89285a6, 2025-05-16, first in v8.10.0; https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/pull/11417) sizes it from the device limit and fixes https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/issues/11389 ('WebGPU broken on some devices'). No 8.9.x patch carries the fix.
evidence.narrowed: Bisected with the pixi.js bundles on the same adapter: 8.2.6, 8.9.0, 8.9.2 and 8.9.2-dev.f4f8fb2 blank; 8.9.2-dev.89285a6 (the merge of #11417), 8.10.0, 8.10.1 and 8.10.2 render. First good release: 8.10.0.
evidence.realGpu: A real GPU renders these versions when its WebGL and WebGPU texture limits agree: the hardware record 2026-10-10-macos-26-apple-m5-max (Apple M5 Max, Metal, isFallbackAdapter false; WebGL reports 16 texture units there) passed 8.2.6 to 8.9.2 on WebGPU with React 18.3.1 and 19.3.0. It is a partial record, so it verifies nothing; it shows the blank render is the #11389 limit mismatch, which this machine's software adapter has and that Mac does not, not WebGPU on 8.2-8.9 as such.

pr.description: Required check: React 18.3 and each React 19 epoch at its latest patch against the minimum and the current Pixi 8, React 18.0 (the lowest React 18 minor) against the Pixi 8 minimum, two Pixi 7 cells (React 18.0 at the Pixi 7 minimum, React 19.3 at the current Pixi 7), plus fast probes at every named Pixi 8 boundary. React 18.1 and 18.2 run nightly (and in their packages' own fixtures).

nightly.description: Full cross-product: every React epoch at its latest patch against every Pixi 8 minor at its latest audited patch and against every audited Pixi 7 release in the Pixi 7 adapter's range (the lowest and highest patch of 7.2 and 7.3, 7.4.2 and 7.4.3), plus every audited probe tuple.

negative.description: The React 19.3 adapter installed beside React 19.1.9 by a consumer that ignores peers (--legacy-peer-deps): its exact peer (19.3.0) would refuse the install, so this checks that the adapter's own environment check still rejects the wrong minor and names the per-minor package to install.
The React 18.3 adapter installed beside React 19.3.0: the strict peer check must refuse the install.

The React 18.0 adapter installed beside React 18.3.1 by a consumer that ignores peers (--legacy-peer-deps): its exact peer (18.0.0) would refuse the install, so this checks that the adapter's own environment check still rejects the other React 18 minor and names the per-minor package to install.
The Pixi 8 adapter beside the excluded pixi.js 8.5.0: the strict peer check refuses the install.
The same pair installed with --legacy-peer-deps (a consumer that ignores peers): the adapter's own environment check must still reject pixi.js 8.5.0.
The Pixi 7 adapter installed beside pixi.js 8.22.0: the strict peer check must refuse the install.

The same pair installed with --legacy-peer-deps (a consumer that ignores peers): the Pixi 7 adapter must still reject pixi.js 8 and name the Pixi 8 adapter. Through require, checkEnvironment rejects it with UNSUPPORTED_TUPLE; through import, the ESM linker already fails, because pixi.js 8 lacks named exports the adapter imports (SimpleMesh, SimpleRope, SimplePlane, FXAAFilter).
